checks.why: a wrapped handler const (`const listUsers = catchAsync(async (req, res) => …)`) handed to a route is registered there, in TypeScript as in JavaScript. The TypeScript graph records no returned-function fact for the wrapper, so the row keeps the name's rung, as for a library wrapper; it was '[by name] … reads it'
want: [by name] users.<module>   src/routes/users.ts:4   — registered as a GET route "/users"

checks.why: CONTROL: a function handler passed directly keeps its route row from the method rule
a schema built by a library, written inside a route's options object (`{ schema: { response: { 200: TaskSchema } } }`), is part of the options, not a handler the router calls: read, never registered
the same for a schema on an options object split over several lines
an options object passed positionally (`router.post('/users', userOptions, listUsers)`) is not callable
the router a module registers routes on is their receiver, not a handler of them
a router mounted with `app.use('/api', api)` is a mount, and the app is the receiver: neither is registered as a route
